01.r: The grain you sow and harvest.
01.n: The Hebrew is plural, 'your seeds', meaning the crops sown; Gesenius lists this very form, citing this verse. It stands first for emphasis, before the verb: 'your seed and your vineyards he will tithe'. The 'your' is plural, addressed to the whole people.

02.r: The vines whose fruit he will also tithe.
t: and of the revenues of your vineyards
02.n: Gesenius gives the first sense as a field set with plants of nobler quality, cultivated as a garden or orchard. The tenth would be taken from their yield; the Douay-Rheims says 'the revenues of your vineyards'.

s: he will take a tenth of
he will take the tithe of
03.r: The king will take one tenth of your produce for himself.
t: And he will take the tenth
And he will take the tenth
And he will take the tenth
And he will take the tenth
03.n: Gesenius: to decimate, that is, to take the tenth part of produce, to tithe, citing this verse; this plain form means to take the tenth, while another form means to give it. So here the tithing is the king's taking, not the people's giving.

04.r: He will pass what he takes to his own men.
04.n: A perfect with 'and', carrying on the future of the verb before it: 'and he will give'. YLT renders the perfect form literally, 'hath given'. The Hebrew gives no object; several translations add 'it'.

05.n: Gesenius: a eunuch, such as Eastern kings set over their women and other offices of the court; the brief's lexicon gives official, eunuch. Whether the king's officials here were literally eunuchs the verse does not say; the KJV and ASV say 'officers'.

06.r: The king's men who serve him at court.
06.n: The word means a slave or servant; Gesenius notes that it is applied to the servants of a king, that is, his ministers. Here the context is royal service, so 'servants' rather than 'slaves'.

01.n: σπέρμα, seed, plural as in the Hebrew.

03.n: ἀποδεκατόω, to tithe, take a tenth: the verb of Jacob's vow in Genesis 28:22 on this page, and of the tithing Pharisees in Matthew 23:23 on this page.

05.n: εὐνοῦχος, eunuch, the source of the English word.
